title: Blood transfusion: indications, administration and reactions (India)
specialty: Transfusion Medicine / Haematology / Internal Medicine / Surgery

evidenceAudit.scope: Safe use of blood components in India: red cell, platelet, plasma and cryoprecipitate triggers and doses, administration, monitoring, and recognition, management and reporting of transfusion reactions under the Haemovigilance Programme of India (HvPI), built on the NIB Good Blood Transfusion Practices Guidance.
findings: Red cell thresholds (Hb 7 g/dL stable adults; 8 g/dL orthopaedic, cardiac surgery or cardiovascular disease; 7 g/dL non-bleeding obstetric), single-unit transfusion, FFP 10–15 mL/kg and INR above 1.5 rule, platelet dose (1 unit per 10 kg) and prophylactic and therapeutic triggers, cryoprecipitate indications, transport, sampling, cannula and filter, infusion rates and maximum times, monitoring schedule, reaction timeline and definitions, management steps and HvPI reporting checked against the NIB Good Blood Transfusion Practices Guidance.
Adrenaline dose for anaphylactic reactions from the WAO 2020 / RCUK 2021 sources used in the Anaphylaxis topic.
unverifiedSections: The opened NIB text was truncated after the adrenaline dose; antipyretic and antihistamine doses are not given there.
Paediatric red cell volume is not in the opened text.
The adrenaline route in the NIB text was cut off; IM dosing is taken from the Anaphylaxis topic sources.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Blood components save lives but carry risks: wrong-blood errors, infection, reactions and fluid overload. Indian guidance favours restrictive red cell transfusion (Hb 7 g/dL in stable adults), single-unit transfusion with reassessment, and plasma and platelets only for defined indications (NIB). Most reactions happen early, so the first 15 minutes are given slowly with close observation. Any suspected reaction means stopping the transfusion, keeping the line open with saline, assessing airway, breathing and circulation, sending samples and the bag to the blood centre, and reporting to HvPI.
keyMechanisms: ABO-incompatible red cells cause intravascular haemolysis, shock and DIC.
Donor leucocyte or cytokine reactions cause febrile non-haemolytic reactions.
Plasma proteins trigger allergic and anaphylactic reactions.
Volume overload (TACO) and donor antibodies (TRALI) cause respiratory distress.

physicalSigns: Temperature 38°C or more with a rise of 1°C (FNHTR) (NIB)
Hypotension: systolic fall 30 mmHg or more to 80 mmHg or less (NIB)
redFlags: Hypotension, hypoxaemia, haemoglobinuria: stop and treat as life-threatening (NIB)
precipitants: Identification errors at sampling or bedside
Rapid transfusion in heart failure, elderly, small patients (TACO)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Pre-existing cardiac disease; responds to diuretic.
New drug given at the same time.
Positive history, not linked to unit.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Fever 38°C or more and a rise of 1°C or more from baseline, no other cause.
Systolic fall of 30 mmHg or more with systolic 80 mmHg or less.
Hypoxaemia (P/F 300 or less, or SpO2 below 90% on air) within 6 hours.
At least 3 listed criteria within 12 hours.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Below 7 g/dL (stable) or below 8 g/dL (cardiac, orthopaedic)

clinicalManagement.title: Decide
actions: Use restrictive thresholds and single units in non-bleeding adults; reassess before more (NIB).
Do not give FFP for volume or nutrition (NIB).

clinicalManagement.title: Administer
actions: Two trained staff (one a doctor) at the bedside check; 170–200 micron filter (NIB).
First 15 minutes at about 1 mL/min; red cells 100–150 mL/hour; complete red cells within 4 hours, platelets and plasma within 30 minutes of start per unit (NIB).
No calcium-containing fluids or 5% dextrose in the line (NIB).

clinicalManagement.title: Suspected reaction
actions: Stop the transfusion; keep IV access with saline via another line (NIB).
Airway, high-flow oxygen; saline to maintain BP (NIB).
Anaphylaxis: adrenaline (see medicines); steroids and bronchodilators as adjuncts (NIB).
Fever or allergy only: antipyretic and antihistamine; do not restart from the same bag (NIB).

clinicalManagement.title: Investigate and report
actions: Record vitals, time, unit number and volume (NIB).
Send samples and bag to the blood centre; complete the reaction form; report to HvPI (NIB).

regimens.frequency: 100–150 mL/hour after a slow first 15 minutes
adjustments: Paediatric: Paediatric volume not in the opened text.
Penicillin allergy: Not an antibiotic; penicillin allergy does not change this medicine.
CKD: Slower rate and diuretic consideration in kidney failure (TACO risk).
CLD: No adjustment.
monitoring: Vitals at 15 minutes and every 30–60 minutes

medicationPlan.note: Component triggers, doses and administration rules from the NIB Good Blood Transfusion Practices Guidance; reactions reported to HvPI. India-only topic; the Saudi topic is unchanged. Not clinically reviewed.

keyPoints: Hb 7 g/dL threshold in stable adults; one unit then reassess.
FFP 10–15 mL/kg only with bleeding or INR above 1.5 before risky procedures.
Platelets 1 unit per 10 kg; prophylaxis below 10,000.
Reaction: stop, keep line open with saline, report to HvPI.
pitfalls: Restarting the same bag after a reaction.

patientEducation: Tell staff at once about fever, itch, breathlessness or pain during transfusion.
lifestyleAndDiet: Treat underlying iron deficiency to reduce need for transfusion.
mdtReferrals: Blood centre medical officer for every reaction
dischargeCriteria: Reaction investigated and reported if one occurred
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Recheck Hb or counts as indicated; document any reaction in the record.
